title: The rate on the card isn't the rate you pay

probes.question: A card quotes 12.99% APR compounded daily. About what is the effective annual rate?
True or false: compounding daily makes the effective annual rate higher than the quoted APR.

image.alt: Illustration of a curve rising slowly and then steeply, with orange coins growing larger along it, like a balance compounding over time

panels.text: Most US credit cards quote an APR, a nominal annual rate. A common example is 12.99%.
The card compounds it daily. Interest is added to the balance each day, and tomorrow's interest is charged on a slightly bigger balance.
Over a year, 12.99% compounded daily works out to an effective annual rate of about 13.87%.
So a $1,000 balance left alone would grow to about $1,139 in a year, before any new purchases or fees.
The twist: for a typical UK card issuer, between 80% and 90% of income from cardholders comes from interest charges.
